wu: Play 'Job Charades': Students act out jobs (teacher, doctor, chef) while others guess, saying 'You are a [job]!'
wuAlt: Play 'What's my job?' with clues like 'You work with numbers'
pres: Show job flashcards (teacher, doctor, chef, engineer) and model Q&A: 'What is your dream job? I want to be a chef.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: Read a short story about different jobs
Use realia (toy doctor kit, chef hat) to introduce jobs
prac: Do 'Job Interview Pairs': Student A asks 'What is your dream job?', Student B answers, then swap. Monitor and model pronunciation.
ls: Listen to a KET-style audio of two friends talking about dream jobs. Students tick the correct job mentioned on their worksheet.
re: Play 'Job Relay': Teams race to write dream jobs on the board after hearing clues like 'You help sick people.'
prod: Conduct 'Dream Job Interviews': Students pair up, ask 3 questions (What job? Why? Where?), and report answers to the class.
rw: Complete a KET-style reading task matching job descriptions to pictures, then write 3 sentences about their own dream job using 'I want to be...'
st: Read 'The Dream Job' story about a child choosing a job, then sing 'What Do You Want to Be?' with actions. Close with 'Today we assessed our English and celebrated our learning. Thank you, class!'
g: Students act out jobs while others guess
Match job flashcards to bingo cards
Teams race to write jobs after clues
Ask classmates about their dream jobs
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short paragraph about their dream job
Support: Use sentence starters like 'I want to be a...'
hw: Practice speaking about your dream job with family
Draw a picture of your dream job and label it
tip: Use peer assessment during interviews to build confidence and mimic real exam conditions, while keeping the tone celebratory.
checklist: I can ask and answer about dream jobs
I can understand short audio about jobs
I can write 3 sentences about my dream job
I can participate in a job interview
I can report what my partner said
I can celebrate my learning progress
